blocks.text: Half-Duplexes vs Full Multi-Family Duplexes in Abbotsford

parts.t: Active duplex listings in Abbotsford fall into two distinct categories on the MLS®: (1) Titled Half-Duplexes (where each side of the building has its own strata or fee-simple PID title, private driveway, garage, and fenced yard, giving you single-family scale without monthly strata management fees); and (2) Full Duplexes on a Single Title (where one buyer acquires both self-contained side-by-side or upper/lower dwellings on a single lot, ideal for dual-income investors or two branches of an extended family).

Most established duplex and half-duplex properties in Abbotsford are located across Central Abbotsford (around Babich, Berry Park, Gladwin Road, and the Historic Downtown perimeter), Clearbrook in Abbotsford West, and McMillan in Abbotsford East. In addition, under the City of Abbotsford's Official Community Plan ('Urban 3 Infill' designation) and provincial Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) zoning updates, many single-family lots on municipal water and sewer now support new duplex, triplex, or fourplex infill construction.

blocks.text: Insurance, Party-Wall Agreements, and Financing for Duplexes

parts.t: When purchasing a half-duplex in Abbotsford, verify how building insurance and roof/exterior maintenance are structured with the neighbouring owner. Because a two-unit strata duplex rarely collects monthly strata fees or holds council meetings, both halves must maintain joint building insurance (or coordinated homeowners policies covering the shared party wall and roof) and follow the standard bylaws of the BC Strata Property Act. When purchasing a full two-unit or four-unit duplex on a single title, verify whether both units are separately metered for BC Hydro and FortisBC gas and confirm municipal building permits for any basement suites.

blocks.text: 7 Common Questions About Abbotsford Duplexes for Sale

parts.t: What is the difference between a half-duplex and a townhome in Abbotsford?

A half-duplex shares only one party wall in a two-unit building and typically has no monthly strata fees, strata council, or pet/rental bylaws beyond standard BC Strata Property Act defaults, whereas a townhome is part of a multi-unit strata corporation with monthly fees.
Where are most duplexes located in Abbotsford?
Duplexes and half-duplexes are primarily found in Central Abbotsford (around Gladwin Road, Babich, Berry Park, and Historic Downtown), Clearbrook in Abbotsford West, and McMillan in Abbotsford East.
Do half-duplexes in Abbotsford pay monthly strata fees?

Most two-unit strata half-duplexes in Abbotsford are self-managed and do not charge monthly strata fees; instead, the two owners split the annual joint building insurance policy and coordinate shared roof or driveway repairs as needed.
Can I build a new duplex on a single-family lot in Abbotsford?

Under the City of Abbotsford Official Community Plan (Urban 3 Infill) and BC's Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) zoning rules, many serviced urban residential lots qualify for duplex or multiplex redevelopment subject to lot width, servicing capacity, and setback bylaws.
Can I use rental income from the second side of a full duplex to qualify for a mortgage?

Yes. When buying a full duplex on a single title—or a half-duplex with a legal basement suite—Canadian lenders typically allow a percentage of the market rent or signed lease income to help qualify your mortgage.
Are utility meters separated on Abbotsford duplexes?

Titled half-duplexes always have separate BC Hydro, FortisBC gas, and municipal water meters. On older full duplexes on a single title, always verify during inspection whether hydro and gas meters are separated or shared.
